Comparison with similar homes
The property's building is assessed at $19.17 per square foot of building area (building AV $20,706 ÷ 1,080
sq ft). The median of 20 similar homes in the same Assessor neighborhood is $12.77 per square foot, so the
property is 50% above the median.
The building part of the assessment is compared, per square foot, because the Assessor values land
separately at a neighborhood rate per square foot of land.
20 of the 20 comparable homes have a building assessed lower per square foot than the property. The
property ranks at the 100th percentile of the comparable homes by building AV per square foot.
How comparable homes were chosen: same neighborhood, class 203, building sqft within ±25%, built within
±15 years (Assessor neighborhood 71280), excluding multi-building parcels and homes without recorded
square footage or a building assessment. The 20 most similar by size, age, baths, lot, design, construction,
basement and distance (the nearer home first when two are equally similar) are listed on page 2.
Uniformity figure
Applying the comparable homes' median building rate of $12.77 per square foot to the property's 1,080
square feet, and adding the property's land AV of $6,294, gives an assessed value of $20,086. That is
$6,914 less than the current assessed value of $27,000.
This compares Cook County assessed values (AV), and the building's AV per square foot, among similar homes, using
public Assessor data. It is not an appraisal and does not estimate what any property would sell for. AssessGap is not
affiliated with Cook County. You file and sign your own appeal.

Filing steps: Cook County Board of Review
PIN 13-33-103-013-0000 · Tax year 2026
Page 3 of 3
AssessGap is not affiliated with Cook County. You file and sign your own appeal.
How a homeowner files their own appeal, from the Board of Review's published instructions and rules (checked
2026-11-24). Rules and dates change; the Board's website is the final word. This is general information, not legal
advice. You file, sign and present your own appeal.
1.
Check when Jefferson Township opens. The Board hasn't posted its dates yet; each township is
open about 30 days. You can pre-register on the Board's portal now. Dates:
https://www.cookcountyboardofreview.com/dates-and-deadlines
2.
Take a color photo of the front of your home. The Board's Rule 14 requires one, taken within the last
12 months, in the brief you upload. Mark the date it was taken. Photos of the comparable homes are
encouraged.
3.
Check the details on page 2 (square feet, year built, bedrooms, baths) against your home. If the
Assessor has something wrong, say so in your brief.
4.
Go to https://appeals.cookcountyboardofreview.com/ and choose Submit an Appeal. You can create
an account or continue as a guest (guests get the decision by mail only; account holders also get it
by email).
5.
Choose "Property Over-Assessed" as the type of appeal and enter PIN 13-33-103-013-0000. When
asked if you are a Board of Review attorney, answer No. Choose your appellant type (owner).
6.
Decide whether you want a hearing. It is optional, held by phone for homeowners, and the Board
says you are not penalized for skipping it. You choose this when you file.
7.
Enter comparable properties if you like (optional: the Board's analysts also pull their own). The
evidence comparables on page 2 are similar homes in your Assessor neighborhood whose building
is assessed lower per square foot than yours; the other homes listed there are not.
8.
Review, initial, confirm and submit before the deadline. Save your complaint number.
9.
Upload your evidence after submitting: your brief with the photo, and this report if you wish, by the
evidence deadline for your township.
10.
Watch for the decision, usually 8–16 weeks after your township closes. You can check status at
https://apps.cookcountyil.gov/BORDecisionSearch/. A re-review must be requested within 3 days of
the decision letter. If you disagree with the decision, you can appeal to the state Property Tax
Appeal Board within 30 days, and you can appeal again next year.
AssessGap is not affiliated with Cook County. You file and sign your own appeal. This compares Cook County assessed
values (AV), and the building's AV per square foot, among similar homes, using public Assessor data. It is not an appraisal
and does not estimate what any property would sell for.
